collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE I: SONGS, CHANTS, SPEECHES AND WELCOMES (LCA-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
Isola sings, chants and speaks for itself: welcoming a new leader, wishing travelers luck, greeting newcomers and newborns, rallying for hard work, standing up for each other, and arguing about who gets the next verse.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: The harvest is in: hold a thanksgiving feast, or store the extra for the dry season.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: It has been the best harvest in years. (subject) wants to hold the great thanksgiving feast, with songs all night and every pot full. (friend) remembers the dry season three years ago, when the stores ran out, and wants to put the extra away instead. What should the village do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: The feast lasts until dawn. There are songs of thanks to the land, the rain, the farmers and, for some reason, a very large pumpkin. Everyone eats far too much. The stores are lower than (friend) would like, and (friend.he/she) does not let anyone forget it.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: The extra is dried, salted and stored away. The village sings a short song of thanks and goes to bed early. Some people are disappointed. But when the dry season comes, the stores last, and (subject) is the first to say (friend) was right.
